PullRequest.Title: agentHost: update Claude Agent SDK to 0.3.304
PullRequest.Body:
Updates the Claude Agent SDK from `0.3.281` to `0.3.304` (current npm `latest`).

## Changes

- Bump the pin in `build/agent-sdk/agents/claude/package.json` and the root `devDependencies`, and refresh both lockfiles.
- **Forward the `thinking-display-updates` beta to CAPI.** SDK 0.3.304 sends `thinking: { type: "adaptive", display: "updates" }` together with `anthropic-beta: thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18`. Our proxy's beta allowlist (`anthropicBetas.ts`) stripped that header, so CAPI rejected the request:
  `400 thinking.adaptive.display: Input should be 'summarized', 'omitted'`
  The SDK then retried without `display`, so users didn't see the error, but every affected turn made an extra failing request. Same endpoint, auth and body, A/B tested against real CAPI:

  | Beta forwarded to CAPI | Result |
  |---|---|
  | No (current allowlist) | 400, then the SDK retries without `display` |
  | Yes | 200 |

  Like the `per-turn-control` fix in #337626, the proxy still only forwards betas the SDK itself sends. It doesn't add betas of its own.
- Re-record `claude-model-changes-between-turns-retain-provider-context`. The only diff is the SDK's new `<local-command-caveat>` wording after `/model`.

## Notes for reviewers

- With `display: "updates"`, the short progress notes the model writes between tool calls arrive as regular `thinking` blocks / `thinking_delta` text (per Anthropic's docs). Reasoning blocks stay empty, as under the previous default (`omitted`). The live and replay mappers already turn these into reasoning parts, so users will now see these progress notes in the reasoning UI.
- No breaking changes in the SDK changelog between 0.3.281 and 0.3.304.

## Validation

- `cd build && node --test agent-sdk/test/versionSync.test.ts`: passed
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run test-node -- --runGlob "**/agentHost/test/node/**/{claude,anthropic,capi}*.test.js"`: passed (830 tests)
- `scripts\test-integration.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\e2e\providers\claudeAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts` (strict replay): passed (132 passing, 40 pending)
- Cross-platform Azure validation, pipeline 111 CI build [487324](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=487324): passed. `Agent SDK: build + upload` and `Run Agent Host E2E tests (Electron)` passed on Windows, Linux and macOS

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a Claude agent turn through the local Anthropic-compatible proxy after upgrading to SDK 0.3.304
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SDK subprocess posts to the local /v1/messages proxy; the proxy parses the request, filters the beta header, and awaits one CAPI messages network stream before deltas can reach the UI. Each returned display-update thinking delta is serialized through local SSE and synchronously mapped/dispatched as an existing ChatReasoning action, but no separate remote request is required for it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: CAPI Anthropic messages request and streamed response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful CAPI request per turn with the SDK 0.3.304 beta forwarded; concurrent sessions can each have an active request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: SDK 0.3.281 made one successful CAPI request per turn without display-update thinking content. The coordinated version bump plus allowlist entry still makes one successful request; omitting the new allowlist entry would instead cause the new SDK's rejected attempt and retry, which this diff avoids.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first response event gates visible turn progress and the stream carries all subsequent response content.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON encode/decode and local SSE forwarding of thinking display-update chunks
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local frame/action per SDK-emitted stream event; newly visible progress notes contribute a bounded number of thinking chunks per turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior SDK/default omitted these progress-note thinking chunks, so they did not incur local SSE serialization or ChatReasoning dispatch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Processing occurs inline with stream consumption, but uses the established incremental delta path and backpressure.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One remote CAPI request per active turn. Additional local serialization and action dispatch scale with the number and byte length of short thinking display-update chunks, which in turn scale with progress notes/tool-call phases rather than transcript history or collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each session owns a long-lived SDK query/subprocess and active sessions can stream concurrently; this PR adds no new concurrency burst or limiter change. Proxy response writes honor backpressure, and turn processing remains sequential within each stream.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no response cache on the turn path. The beta filter is evaluated once per inbound request over the bounded SDK beta-header list. SDK module loading is memoized after first load.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the request and event paths: the added allowlist line is reached once per /v1/messages request, proxy code performs one CAPI call, and thinking_delta maps directly to ChatReasoning. The external SDK's exact emission policy is opaque in-repository, so no stronger performance claim is justified.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number and size of model-generated display updates is not established by repository code, but they are described and handled as short incremental progress notes. No evidence shows enough additional events to cause latency, throughput loss, or dropped frames, and the change avoids an entire failed remote attempt.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added stream work is incremental and bounded on an existing path, while forwarding the matching beta prevents a full failed request/retry cycle that would be materially more expensive.

Scenarios.Scenario: First Claude use after a shipped SDK version upgrade, and subsequent warm uses
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the first Claude SDK API call can proceed, the service resolves the versioned SDK root. On a cold 0.3.304 cache it downloads one platform tarball, writes and extracts it, then imports sdk.mjs; on a warm cache it checks the .complete sentinel and imports/memoizes the module.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the platform-specific Claude SDK tarball from the configured CDN
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced download per process for claude/0.3.304/platform on a cold cache; zero on warm cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An installation already warm for 0.3.281 used that version's cache. Shipping 0.3.304 necessarily selects a new version-keyed artifact and causes one cold fetch before becoming warm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold download and extraction block the first SDK load; warm cache resolution is a sentinel check.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write tarball, extract SDK tree, write sentinel, atomically publish cache, and import sdk.mjs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write/extract/publish sequence per cold version/target; one sentinel existence check per pre-memoization resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent work occurred when 0.3.281 was first installed; already-warm 0.3.281 installations did not need another artifact until this version bump.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold extraction/import gates first use; subsequent module calls return the memoized binding.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One artifact for the current platform/version. Cost scales with the single tarball size (repository comments place these artifacts around 70-95 MB), not with sessions or turns after the module is loaded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-process callers coalesce on one promise keyed by cacheDir; cross-window races may each fetch but converge through an atomic rename, behavior unchanged by this diff. Once loaded, _sdkModule avoids repeated resolution/download within the process.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The cache key includes package id, SDK version, and target. Existing 0.3.281 caches do not satisfy 0.3.304, so the first use after upgrade is cold; later uses hit the .complete sentinel. Failures are negatively cached for 30 seconds.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in version-keyed cold/warm behavior and coalescing from the downloader implementation; low evidence for any changed artifact-size cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact 0.3.304 tarball size versus 0.3.281 is not present in the diff, so there is no evidence of a size or extraction-cost regression beyond the expected one-time cache miss for a new version.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. A one-time version-keyed download is inherent to deploying the requested SDK update, remains coalesced and persistently cached, and the diff provides no evidence that the artifact or extraction work materially increased.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build and publish platform-specific Claude SDK artifacts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CI runs npm ci for the pinned package, verifies/imports the staged SDK, creates a tarball, computes its hash, and on publish performs a CDN HEAD followed by upload only when absent. This work is off the end-user interaction path but on the release-build path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: npm ci and SDK load-probe subprocess
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One npm install and one load probe per produced Claude target, unchanged from 0.3.281.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same commands ran for 0.3.281 with the same dependency shape and one optional native package per target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks that platform's artifact production but is off product runtime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stage files, tar node_modules, hash artifact, and remove staging directory
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One staging/tar/hash cycle per Claude target, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks artifact completion but not user startup or turns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Registry package download during npm ci and CDN HEAD/upload on publish
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Registry fetches for the base SDK and one applicable optional native package; one CDN HEAD and at most one upload per target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same boundary cardinality for 0.3.281; URLs and integrity values changed, with no added dependency nodes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Claude artifact per applicable platform/architecture job, alongside the unchanged set of SDKs; dependency version changes bytes but not target count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: produce.ts builds applicable SDKs with Promise.all, unchanged by this diff. Each sdk/target has one producer; CDN upload is sequential after its build and guarded by HEAD/idempotency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: npm uses the lockfile; CDN objects are content-addressed by SDK version/target and a matching existing object skips upload. A new 0.3.304 path is cold once, then publish reruns can skip.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that build boundary cardinality and concurrency are unchanged based on the complete lockfile and packaging code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Package byte-size differences are not shown. Lockfiles retain the same package topology, so only versioned artifact contents may differ.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The SDK bump changes artifact identities but adds no dependency fan-out, target fan-out, or new build boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Replay the /model command in the Claude model-change E2E capture
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed YAML is test replay input only; it does not run in production or add work to the live model-switch path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One changed caveat string in one recorded test exchange.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No product cache behavior is affected.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed-file role and hunk content.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the diff is fixture text only.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and every diff page. Traced the turn network/stream path, reasoning-action fan-out, SDK cold/warm cache lifecycle, and build packaging/upload boundaries. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced; no findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
